record.context_brief: Chebyshev positivity for even convex majorants
record.original_question: If mu is a nonnegative continuous even convex function on [-1,1], must the snake polynomials associated with mu have a nonnegative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind?

evidence.quote: Conjecture (G.N.) If mu >= 0 is a continuous even convex function in [-1, 1], then the associated with mu snake polynomials have non-negative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T_k(x) = \cos(k\arccos x)$, $k=0,1,2,\ldots$, denote the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind on $[-1,1]$.

For a continuous function $\mu:[-1,1]\to[0,\infty)$ and an integer $n\ge 1$, the associated "snake polynomial" of degree $n$ is the (unique) algebraic polynomial $P_n$ of degree at most $n$ that satisfies $|P_n(x)|\le \mu(x)$ for all $x\in[-1,1]$ and that equioscillates against the majorant $\mu$ in the sense that there exist points $-1\le x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_n\le 1$ with
$$P_n(x_j) = (-1)^{n-j}\mu(x_j),\qquad j=0,1,\ldots,n,$$
i.e. $P_n$ touches the upper envelope $+\mu$ and the lower envelope $-\mu$ alternately at $n+1$ consecutive points of $[-1,1]$.

Each such polynomial admits a unique expansion
$$P_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} c_k(n,\mu)\, T_k(x).$$

Prove or disprove the following statement: if $\mu$ is a nonnegative, continuous, even, and convex function on $[-1,1]$, then for every $n\ge 1$ all coefficients of the snake polynomial in the Chebyshev basis of the first kind are nonnegative, i.e.
$$c_k(n,\mu)\ge 0\qquad\text{for all }k=0,1,\ldots,n.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a 2023 collection of open problems from the "Hausdorff Geometry of Polynomials" workshop in Sofia, where it is explicitly labeled a conjecture. No published resolution (proof or counterexample) was located in subsequent literature, so the problem appears to remain open.
